hypotheses.justification: The theorem takes this instance only because `ι` is one of its arguments. The statement never uses it. The sum `∑ k, …` needs only `[Fintype ι]`. `db b k` is defined as `CartierDual.ofDual O H (b.coord k)`, which needs no decidability, and `db` does not take the instance: `db_apply`, whose statement mentions `db b k`, compiles under `omit [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] in`. The conclusion contains no `if`, so nothing in it depends on which decidability instance is chosen. The proof uses the instance only inside `hcoef`: in the `if i = k then 1 else 0` of `hdb` (from `db_apply_basis`) and in `Finset.sum_ite_eq'`. Both lemmas accept any `DecidableEq` instance, so starting the proof with `classical` (with `omit [DecidableEq ι] in`) makes the same proof go through unchanged.
